comparisons.peer_topic: Commercial Paper Program Structure and Status
comparisons.peer_summary: The Company established a commercial paper program on November 3, 2022, allowing for unsecured notes up to $3 billion with maturities up to 397 days, but had no commercial paper outstanding as of December 28, 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both Broadcom and AMD disclose specific commercial paper program terms including principal limits, maturity lengths, and zero outstanding balances. Broadcom limits its program to $2 billion with maturities up to 397 days and had no commercial paper outstanding as of November 3, 2024 (avgo_2024_8_P157_S001, avgo_2024_8_P157_S005). Similarly, AMD’s program allows up to $3 billion in unsecured notes with maturities up to 397 days, and AMD had no commercial paper outstanding as of December 28, 2024 (amd_2024_8_P094_S001, amd_2024_8_P094_S003). Both companies structure their paper to be sold at a discount or at par with market-driven interest rates (avgo_2024_8_P157_S002, amd_2024_8_P094_S002).

sentences.text: We have a commercial paper program pursuant to which we may issue unsecured commercial paper notes ("Commercial Paper") in principal amount of up to $2 billion outstanding at any time with maturities of up to 397 days from the date of issue.
We had no Commercial Paper outstanding at either November 3, 2024 or October 29, 2023.

On November 3, 2022, the Company established a commercial paper program, under which the Company may issue unsecured commercial paper notes up to a maximum principal amount outstanding at any time of $3 billion with a maturity of up to 397 days from the date of issue.
During 2024 and 2023, the Company did not issue any commercial paper under the program and as of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023, the Company had no commercial paper outstanding.

comparisons.peer_topic: Commercial Paper Authorization and Outstanding Balance
comparisons.peer_summary: The company has Board authorization to borrow up to $10.0 billion under its commercial paper program, with no commercial paper outstanding as of both December 28, 2024, and December 30, 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both Broadcom and Intel disclose commercial paper program authorizations and confirm that no commercial paper was outstanding at the end of fiscal year 2024. Broadcom’s program authorizes up to $2 billion in unsecured notes, with no outstanding balances as of November 3, 2024 (avgo_2024_8_P157_S001, avgo_2024_8_P157_S005). Intel has a Board authorization to borrow up to $10.0 billion, also with no commercial paper outstanding as of December 28, 2024 (intc_2024_8_P151_S001, intc_2024_8_P151_S002). While the authorized amounts differ significantly ($2B vs $10B), the structural status of having zero outstanding commercial paper is a direct similarity.

comparisons.peer_topic: Revolving Credit Facility Availability and Status
comparisons.peer_summary: As of August 29, 2024, no amounts were outstanding under the Revolving Credit Facility, with $2.50 billion available. The facility matures in May 2026, and borrowed amounts may be prepaid without penalty.
comparisons.comparison: The target disclosure discusses a commercial paper program that impacts borrowing capacity under a revolving credit facility. While Micron (MU) does not disclose a commercial paper program in the supplied text, it discloses the status of its revolving credit facility, which is the related funding source mentioned by Broadcom. Broadcom notes that outstanding commercial paper reduces the availability under its revolving credit facility (avgo_2024_8_P157_S004), whereas Micron explicitly states that $2.50 billion was available under its Revolving Credit Facility with no amounts outstanding as of August 29, 2024 (mu_2024_8_P061_S001). Both disclosures address liquidity resources and unutilized borrowing capacity, but the specific instrument (commercial paper vs. direct revolving credit availability) differs.
